title: Equipment you can afford to go cheap on for your home gym
summary: Five areas where home gym owners can save money without hurting their training: weight plates (buy cheapest in good condition, e.g. from closing gyms), clamps (hardware-store clamps), wooden blocks, DIY platforms, and stations bought used or negotiated directly with a sales rep for a cheaper non-commercial model.

claims.claim: Weight is weight: don't worry about plate brand, looks or shine; buy the cheapest plates in the best condition you can find.
Your best bet for cheap plates is small mom-and-pop gyms that are closing and selling everything.
Once you lift in the 400-500 lb range consider calibrated plates: cheap 45s can actually weigh 38-48 lbs, which can create a dangerous ~20 lb side-to-side discrepancy on a 400 lb squat.
He bought close to 1,000 lbs of plates, going for the cheapest, so he owns a mismatch of brands; companies discount bundles and each brand tends to be cheapest on different plate sizes.
$2 hardware-store clamps work as well as or better than barbell collars, except for dumbbell tricep movements where pressure on the plate can make them fly off.
Don't buy wooden blocks (for block pulls, box squats) from fitness companies at about five times the price; have a hardware store build them or build them yourself.
Build your own lifting platform: small branded platforms cost around $1,000 while you can build one for under $150.
His 16 x 8 ft multi-layer platform with stall mats cost about $500 to build; custom-made it would have cost at least $4,000, ten times more.

Never buy stations (cable machines, preacher curls) at commercial list price: buy used, or contact a wholesaler's sales rep directly, ask for a cheaper non-commercial model (often half price), and negotiate free shipping.
Saving money on equipment may mean waiting two or three months for shipping; patience is the price.
Following these five tips can save $3,000-4,000 on a home or garage gym.
'Buy nice or buy twice' applies to gym equipment, with a few exceptions where going cheap is fine.
